edges.scope: Geometric-sequence subcase only: each fixed q in (0,1) has arbitrarily large-measure compact sets avoiding every affine copy of {q^n}; Lean scope covers q=1/2.
edges.missing_hypotheses: General infinite sets; simultaneous avoidance across q; geometric manuscript proof audit.

edges.scope: Any infinite A containing an affine copy of a fixed geometric sequence inherits the avoidance conclusion, since an affine copy of A would contain an affine copy of that sequence.
edges.missing_hypotheses: This sufficient structural condition need not hold for arbitrary infinite A.

edges.scope: Nine-dimensional Borsuk counterexample; improves the dimension surface of an already-disproved conjecture.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Local audit of rank-one-projector compact-set construction; not a new resolution of the general existence claim.

edges.scope: No proper arbitrary five-coloring of the Euclidean plane and a seven-color upper bound, hence 6<=chi<=7.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Distinguishing 6 from 7; no explicit small finite six-chromatic unit-distance graph extracted.

edges.scope: A six-chromatic finite subgraph exists by graph-coloring compactness, but does not force independence ratio below 1/5.
edges.missing_hypotheses: An independence/fractional-coloring certificate, not merely a chromatic lower bound.

edges.scope: Every positive-integer set with divergent reciprocal sum contains APs of every finite length.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Local theorem/proof audit.

edges.scope: Odd cycle lengths in an infinite-chromatic graph have divergent reciprocal sum by local P57; therefore they contain APs of every finite length, with positive even difference.
edges.missing_hypotheses: No common-vertex condition or finite graph bound; no novelty claim.

edges.scope: The quantitative progression-free bound gives a uniform finite harmonic-mass bound for every fixed k, by dyadic summation.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Effective dependence on k and a numerical optimum; the reciprocal comparator alone is not a numeric f(k) bound.

edges.scope: A one-sided progression-free upper bound does not provide the requested asymptotic equivalent.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Matching lower bound with ratio tending to one; effective constants before finite cells.

edges.scope: Asymptotic progression-free estimates do not decide the exact next finite r_3 cell.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Explicit finite bound tight at target N, or witness/nonexistence certificate.

edges.scope: Divergence of the reciprocal sum of primes implies APs of arbitrary length via F159.
edges.missing_hypotheses: This reproves the ordinary AP conclusion, not consecutive-prime APs; novelty is not claimed.

edges.scope: For fixed r>=2, W(r,k)>k^{k floor(log2 r)/100000} eventually, so W(r,k)^(1/k) tends to infinity.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Unknown absolute threshold K and local proof audit; W(2,7) not determined.

edges.scope: Combining the lower bound W(2,k)>k^{k/100000} with the atlas inequality f(k)>=0.5 log W(2,k) gives f(k)>=k log k/200000 eventually.
edges.missing_hypotheses: This recovers an already-known growth shape with weaker constant; not a new record.

edges.scope: Ryser constructions are intersecting r-uniform families with covering number r, hence admissible objects for the f(r) minimization.
edges.missing_hypotheses: No O(r) edge count or explicit small-r witness is supplied; thresholds existential, and P21 already solved asymptotically.

edges.scope: For every finite coloring and finite k, a k-element positive-integer set has all nonempty subset sums and products in one color.
edges.missing_hypotheses: No Lean scope linked; manuscript proof audit.

edges.scope: Arbitrarily large finite sets with monochromatic sums and products do not automatically assemble into a single infinite set.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A compatible nested construction or additional compactness argument; finite sets can escape to infinity.

edges.scope: For each fixed d>=3, every n-point subset of R^d determines >=c_d n^(2/d) distances, stronger than the requested exponent up to o(1).
edges.missing_hypotheses: No Lean scope; proof audit and constants depend on d.

edges.scope: The d=3 lower bound n^(2/3) applies to convex-polyhedron vertices but is weaker than the desired nearly n/2 bound.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Use convexity to obtain a linear lower bound.

edges.scope: F166 fixes d and lets n grow; the few-distance problem fixes the number of distances and lets d grow.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Uniform control of c_d with d; asymptotic regimes cannot be interchanged.

edges.scope: Uniform planar unit-distance upper bound C n^beta for an absolute beta<4/3 improves the upper-bound surface.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Does not reverse the already recorded disproof of n^(1+o(1)); numerical beta and C not extracted.

edges.scope: Almost every pin has >=n^(1-epsilon) distances; this does not reach n/sqrt(log n).
edges.missing_hypotheses: Sharper logarithmic loss control at the planar distinct-distance scale.

edges.scope: General planar O(n^beta), beta<4/3, applies to convex sets but need not imply O(n).
edges.missing_hypotheses: Convexity-specific linear bound.

edges.scope: Rescaling any positive distance to one gives f(d)<=C n^beta uniformly in d; hence the largest-minus-second-largest multiplicity gap is also <=C n^beta.
edges.missing_hypotheses: No matching lower bound or novelty claim; beta<4/3 is existential.

edges.scope: Elementary positivity for chromatic quasisymmetric functions of natural unit interval graphs does not imply unimodality of independence polynomials of arbitrary trees.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Different graph class and polynomial; an actual coefficient-preserving transform and unimodality theorem are required.

edges.scope: Sharp logarithmic exponent s-2 for every fixed s>=5 strengthens the polynomial lower-bound surface in the existing off-diagonal Ramsey problem.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Scope excludes s=3,4; fixed-s constants/thresholds and proof audit.

edges.scope: Diagonal s=t growth is not a fixed-s regime.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A theorem in the target parameter regime with the target quantitative conclusion.

edges.scope: Asymptotic existence bounds are not an explicit algorithmic construction.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A theorem in the target parameter regime with the target quantitative conclusion.

edges.scope: The scope begins at s=5; P166 concerns s=4.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A theorem in the target parameter regime with the target quantitative conclusion.

edges.scope: P544 concerns s=3 and consecutive gaps; neither follows.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A theorem in the target parameter regime with the target quantitative conclusion.

edges.scope: Near-diagonal t=s and t=s+1 are not fixed-s asymptotics.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A theorem in the target parameter regime with the target quantitative conclusion.

edges.scope: A logarithmic exponent with unspecified o(1) does not alone force ratios at consecutive t to tend to one.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A theorem in the target parameter regime with the target quantitative conclusion.

edges.scope: Absolute C gives R(Q_n)<=C 2^n.
edges.missing_hypotheses: No Lean scope linked; manuscript proof audit.

edges.scope: A two-color host of C*2^n vertices may find a cube in either color; P1035 demands one in a specified dense graph on exactly 2^n vertices.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Remove host slack and force the designated color.

edges.scope: Tensor-field classification of Euclidean Ramsey configurations, with spherical non-Ramsey examples and sufficient criteria.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Comparator definition audit for affine-span reductions; no efficient decision algorithm inferred.

edges.scope: Ramsey configurations are guaranteed in some sufficiently high ambient dimension, whereas P173 fixes the plane and two colors.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A dimension-two theorem with the required uniform triangle assertion.

edges.scope: A thin spanning tree has no prescribed isomorphism type; Gyárfás packing asks for a perfect edge decomposition into every prescribed tree tuple.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Prescribed trees, exact edge usage, and simultaneous packing.

edges.scope: Every fixed-degree d graph has independence number at least n/(d+1), so fixed-degree Ramanujan outputs cannot have independent sets O(log n).
edges.missing_hypotheses: A growing-degree transformation with jointly controlled algorithmic cost and clique/independence bounds; source exponent and threshold depend on fixed d.

edges.scope: Hamiltonicity for cubic bipartite planar 3-connected graphs neither ensures all cycle lengths nor applies to all candidate pancyclic graphs; bipartite graphs lack odd cycles.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Pancyclicity in the correct graph class, not Hamiltonicity alone.

edges.scope: Every finite simple graph has an edge partition into O(n) cycles and singleton edges.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Optimal absolute constant and local proof audit.

edges.scope: Splitting each cycle gives O(n) paths, but does not achieve the target ceil(n/2); stronger linear path bounds already exist.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Sharp constant and edge-disjoint path organization.

edges.scope: Cycles/singletons are not prescribed tree components.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Exact tree-shape packing; neither graph decomposability nor matching edge count suffices.

edges.scope: A square-difference-free positive-integer set has finite harmonic mass by |A cap [N]|<=C N^(1-c). Thus odd cycle lengths in an infinite-chromatic graph contain two lengths differing by a positive square, necessarily an even square.
edges.missing_hypotheses: No constraints on shared vertices or a numerical bound.

edges.scope: Every fixed-K_r-free graph, r>=4, with average degree d>=2 has alpha>=c_r n log d/d; paper explicitly identifies P802.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Local proof audit; effective c_r not given.

edges.scope: An independence bound depending on average degree is not the sharp triangle-free chromatic constant or a smallest six-chromatic graph certificate.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Sharp coloring transfer and explicit finite graph/nonexistence evidence.

edges.scope: Random triangle removal from K_n concerns a dense random process; near-Turan deterministic triangle packing needs a uniform theorem for arbitrary prescribed input G.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Correct initial graph, deterministic uniformity, and second-order packing count.

edges.scope: Exact R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1 for m>=n>=3 except (3,3); that exception equals 6.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Local proof audit; full stated parameter range matches P551.

edges.scope: The theorem requires cycle length m>=clique order n; P159 fixes m=4 and lets n grow.
edges.missing_hypotheses: A result for the reversed regime n>m, not the diagonal strip.

edges.scope: A quantitative van der Waerden upper bound can control AP length versus step; all-fixed-k Szemeredi estimates are a potential input.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Explicit uniform dependence on k and an argument yielding infinitely many distinct steps; fixed-k statements alone are insufficient.

edges.scope: The number of systems of distinct representatives equals the number of 0/1 contingency tables: k rows of margin 1, one dummy row of margin ell-k, ell columns of margin 1; forbidden incidence cells have bound 0. F115 therefore supplies an FPRAS for assignment multiplicity.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Assume ell>=k, otherwise no injection exists. This estimates a fixed finite instance; a universal Hall theorem for all intervals is still absent.

edges.scope: A faster maximum-matching algorithm may accelerate finite interval tests on the existing incidence graph.
edges.missing_hypotheses: The source algorithm has success probability >=2/3, not a guaranteed negative certificate; preserve independently verified assignments and Hall obstructions. No asymptotic universal existence theorem follows.

edges.scope: Worst-case subset-sum decision could support a finite sum-distinct candidate screen after an exact collision-search reduction is specified.
edges.missing_hypotheses: P1 concerns collisions between two subsets, not one specified target; algorithm has bounded error, no direct extremal bound, and practical crossover unknown. P1 is already marked solved-upstream locally.

edges.scope: Fast mixing within a fixed graphical degree sequence could diversify degree-controlled test inputs.
edges.missing_hypotheses: The chain samples all simple realizations, not only connected trees; conditioning may be inefficient. Sampling is not exhaustive and supplies no universal unimodality proof.

edges.scope: Fixed-degree graph sampling could supply diverse candidate graphs for an independent pancyclicity verifier.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Pancyclicity is not preserved by switches, and no lower bound on candidate success probability or optimality certificate follows.

edges.scope: Exact field-arithmetic matrix multiplication may inform future rank-computation backends for carry-product certificates.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Arithmetic exponent is not bit complexity, and current matrices are small. It does not overcome certified cone infeasibility or create a working construction.

edges.scope: Subsequential exact-complex DFT circuit savings are computational complexity statements, not cancellation bounds for the squarefree variance or signed mixed moment.
edges.missing_hypotheses: All-length usable algorithms, bit/error control, and the missing analytic estimate remain separate.

edges.scope: Derandomization applies to bounded-error polynomial-time logarithmic-workspace machines.
edges.missing_hypotheses: An explicit Ramsey construction requires an appropriate log-space sampler/search reduction and quantitative clique/independence guarantee; these are not supplied.

edges.scope: Deterministic dense polynomial factorization over F_p is not integer factorization or a theorem excluding the P699 smooth-part residual.
edges.missing_hypotheses: An arithmetic obstruction connecting polynomial factors to actual positional divisibilities is absent.

edges.scope: Random k-SAT limiting thresholds concern independent random clauses with replacement, not structured AP-free-set CNFs at a specified finite N.
edges.missing_hypotheses: Correct instance distribution, a finite-size rate, and a deterministic proof object. Even a typical-case UNSAT probability is not an UNSAT certificate.

edges.scope: Generic Max-Cut approximation hardness does not contradict a theorem guaranteeing a large bipartite subgraph of every triangle-free graph.
edges.missing_hypotheses: The reductions do not certify the triangle-free restriction or identify the extremal value of the target family; hardness and guaranteed bounds are different quantifiers.

edges.scope: P150 is about counts of minimal vertex cuts; F190 concerns induced ordered binary-matrix pattern removal.
edges.missing_hypotheses: No reduction exists in this review; the shared word removal was a lexical false positive.
